newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps fluctuate.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable, swaps fluctuate.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in late trading on Thursday but the swap market was jolted briefly on spillover from the ringgit.
Dealers said overall trading was slow and the only factor of note was the spillover from the Malaysian ringgit.
Spot rupiah was at 2,427.4/27.7 at 0900 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,428.5/29.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,426.5/26.8 and 2,427.5/27.65, respectively.
One local bank dealer said six-month swaps rose to a high of 84.5 points before they were sold down to 80.0/82.0 later.
"There was talk in the market that Bank Negara had called for a meeting with local banks, prompting players to speculate about a Thai-style squeeze," one dealer in Singapore said.
He said there were rumours in the market that Malaysia could copy Thai steps to set up a two-tier market to fend off speculation on its currency.
"Offshore operators immediately drew a parallel with the rupiah and this triggered purchase of six-month swaps."
He said, however, operators reversed some of their holdings after realising liquidity was ample. Overnight money fell to four percent from 11.0 percent in the morning.
The dealer said some players were also selling spot dollars when unloading swaps high, building short dollar positions in the forward market.
Dealers said there were still fears of a Thai-style squeeze in the Jakarta swap market although the central bank has denied plan for a similar move.
"The underlying tone is still biddish for swaps. Offshore operators are tending to extend long forward rupiah positions," the Singapore bank dealer said.
Overnight swap was at 0.3/0.4 and tom/next at 0.9/1.0.
One European bank dealer said local players were now buyers of short-term swaps while offshore was selling with the positions reversed in the forward market on the Thai factor.
Dealers said there was no immediate implication on dollar-rupiah from the volatile dollar-yen market. Indonesia has set a dollar-yen rate at 110 for its 1997/98 budget.
One-month swaps edged up to 13.0/13.5 from 12.50/13.25, two to 26.5/28.5 from 25.0/26.0, three to 40.0/42.0 from 38.5/39.5 and six to 80.0/81.0 from 78.5/80.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,421/2,613 and its conversion band also by one point to 2,421/2,469 on Thursday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
